input:
Let ā = 2î + ĵ - 2k̂ and b̄ = î + ĵ. If c̄ is a vector such that ā · c̄ = |c̄|, |c̄ - ā| = 2√2 and the angle between (ā × b̄) and c̄ is π/6, then |(ā × b̄) × c̄| is

Options:
A. 3/2
B. 2/3
C. 1
D. 3/4

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given vectors ā = 2î + ĵ - 2k̂ and b̄ = î + ĵ, with conditions ā·c̄ = |c̄|, |c̄ - ā| = 2√2, and the angle between (ā × b̄) and c̄ equal to π/6, compute |(ā × b̄) × c̄|.

given_information.angle: θ = π/6 between (ā × b̄) and c̄

phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Square |c̄ - ā| = 2√2 to get |c̄|² + |ā|² - 2(ā·c̄) = 8. Substitute |ā| = 3 and ā·c̄ = |c̄| to find |c̄| = 1. Then compute |ā × b̄| and use the magnitude of vector cross product formula.

key_concepts: Vector cross product magnitude: |u × v| = |u| |v| sin θ
Cross product calculation: î, ĵ, k̂ components

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: First calculate |c̄| using the given magnitude equation, then calculate |ā × b̄|, and finally apply the cross product magnitude formula with sin(π/6).
